speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For over five decades, SportSG has led the development of a vibrant sporting culture in Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Together, we have achieved significant progress in two areas; first, participation in sports; and second, sporting excellence.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In the last decade, SportSG has achieved a significant increase in participation in sports in a number of ways.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: First, in partnership with the Ministry of Education (MOE), we have effectively embedded sports programmes across mainstream and special education schools and expanded the outreach of sports to the young very significantly.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The School Sports Partnership programme, which allows more children to be exposed to multi-sport experiences at introductory and intermediate levels regardless of their skills and abilities, has grown from 19 in 2020 to 92 schools today.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: These programmes expose our youths to diverse sporting experiences, nurtures a love for sports and builds a strong foundation for active and healthy lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Outside of schools, we engage our youths through ActiveSG's academies and clubs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: These offer structured sports programmes for our children to pursue their sporting interests and form bonds and networks with peers beyond schools.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And together with our affiliated partners' programmes, we reach out to about 15,000 regular participants each year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And we want that passion for sport to continue beyond the school years.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: To help them stay connected with sports for life, the ActiveSG Sport Interest Groups provide avenues for Singaporeans to continue to pursue their sporting interests together.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This also allows them to form new friendships and meet others of different ages and abilities to play sport together regularly.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Today, SportSG offers more than 3,000 interest group programmes annually, reaching close to 30,000 participants.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Second, we have increased access to sports through our expansion of sports infrastructure.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In addition to rejuvenating and building new ActiveSG Sport Centres with an expanded offering of sports facilities, we have also built more sports facilities closer to residents' homes through Sport-in-Precinct programmes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Where we can, we have integrated them with government facilities in our heartlands to provide Singaporeans with a one-stop facility to live, work and play, such as at Our Tampines Hub, Bukit Canberra and Heartbeat at Bedok.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have also rejuvenated several others such as the Delta Sport Centre and ActiveSG Sport Parks at Teck Ghee and Bedok North.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: More than 1.9 million Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents have also signed up to the new web-based MyActiveSG+ platform for facility and programme booking since its launch in 2024.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Many more Singaporeans now adopt active and healthy lifestyles.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And this is a big step in our effort to bring our health-span closer to our life-span, and to help Singaporeans live longer, healthier lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Beyond physical fitness activities, mind sports and e-sports have also seen strong growth in participation and recognition both here in Singapore and globally.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We hosted the World Chess Championship for the first time in 2024.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In schools, around 1,700 students competed at the 75th National Schools Individual Chess Championship in the same year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: That is about a 20% increase compared to 2022, which was when it was last held.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As for e-sports, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) region is one of the world's fastest growing e-sports markets.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The upcoming 2026 Asian Games will also feature an increased number of 11 medals for e-sport titles, up from seven at the 2022 Asian Games.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: So, in line with young Singaporeans' widening interest in e-sports, we partnered the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to host the inaugural Olympic Esports Week in 2023.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our Team Singapore e-sport athletes also achieved medal success at the Southeast Asian Games (SEA Games) and other competitions such as at the World Taekwondo Virtual Championships.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In terms of sporting excellence, we have progressively strengthened our High Performance Sport (HPS) ecosystem to nurture more Team Singapore athletes and help them realise their full sporting potential to perform better in more sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Just last month, we celebrated Team Singapore's achievements at the SEA Games in Thailand.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: At the games, our athletes also achieved many firsts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Calvin Quek and Avvir Tham won our first gold in 60 years in the 400 metres hurdles and diving respectively.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Marissa Hafezan won Singapore's first SEA Games karate medal since 2011 and first gold medal since 1993.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our men's 3x3 basketball team won a historic silver medal with a young team averaging just 21 years old.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And I am also happy to report that about half of our athletes who competed for the first time won medals, including some of our youngest Team Singapore athletes, 12-year-old sailor Anya Zahedi and 14-year-old swimmer Julia Yeo.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Julia was just sitting behind Nominated Member Dr Kenneth Goh and myself, and cheering on the Team Singapore athletes one moment, and the next moment she was in the water.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Well, she set her personal best in the backstroke during the womens' 4x100 metres medley relay, and together with her teammates Ting Wen, Jing Wen and Letitia, broke the meet record and won the Gold medal.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And all this while she was swimming in borrowed goggles and swimsuit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And it was Singaporeans' support for our athletes at the games that made all the difference.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Whether it was Singaporeans who were supporting the team from back home or Singaporeans who went to Thailand to cheer on the team, like our Team Nila volunteers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Whether it was cheering the mens' water polo team through their dominant wins in the pool, enroute to their 29th gold medal or our netball teams' heartbreaking three-point loss in the finals, Singaporeans stood with Team Singapore through both victories and defeats.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our supporters embodied the very essence of the Singapore Spirit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: On the fields and in the stadiums, we were united as one voice, cheering as one nation for Team Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As our Team Nila volunteer Mr Andy Toh aptly put, the journey with Team Nila in Bangkok was both poignant and fulfilling, marked by the emotional highs and lows of witnessing athletes' triumphs and disappointments.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: At the highest levels, our athletes have also showed that we have what it takes to do well at the Olympics and the Paralympics.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: They also broke two national records and had two personal bests.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have also stepped up to host top-tier international sporting competitions, testing our capabilities against stronger and more established nations, and rallying our nation's support for our athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For close to three months in 2025, we worked to host the World Aquatics Championships, World Aquatics Masters Championships and the World Para Swimming Championships.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We welcomed over 9,000 international athletes, including the world's top swimmers to Singapore across these events.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We saw outstanding performances from our swimmers like Yip Pin Xiu and Gan Ching Hwee who achieved medal success and broke national records.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our TeamSG para-swimmer Wong Zhi Wei fondly recounted his experience at the World Para Swimming Championships in September last year.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: He said, and I quote, "I was really grateful for the crowd because every time I came up to breathe I could hear them say "Go!" and I could hear a lot of them shouting my name so I am really glad for the support that I have especially for this meet that is held on home ground." Through the years, our athletes and para-athletes do more than just make Singapore proud.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: They show our youth what is possible when they dare to dream.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And we are committed to nurture more youths to turn their dreams into reality.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our achievements so far, both in participation in sports and in sporting excellence, gives us confidence that we are on the right track.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: First, we want to continue to build up our high-performance sports systems to nurture our athletes to their fullest potential.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For our athletes, we are investing in a new home for Team Singapore as part of the Kallang Alive Masterplan.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will integrate all elements of our hardware – our high performance sporting development and sports science system – under one roof for athletes to stay, train, study and compete, supported by the High Performance Sport Institute and the National Sports Associations (NSAs).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will also continue to improve our software, to start organising ourselves around an integrated structure to enhance the end-to-end development of our athletes from youth to adult, so that our athletes can be supported holistically.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And we will continue to refine our sporting policies and programmes to ensure that athletes have the right infrastructure, adequate resources and multiple opportunities to excel.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This reflects our concerted, strategic and long-term commitment to build a sustainable and thriving sports ecosystem for all our athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Second, we will continue to make sport more accessible and inclusive for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We announced the refreshed Disability Sports Master Plan (DSMP) in 2024.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The DSMP lays out our vision to build an inclusive and vibrant sporting landscape where persons of all abilities will have ample opportunities to participate in sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: One of the key moves is the launch of the Enabling Sports Fund to support community-led programmes that make sport accessible, inclusive and meaningful for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Similarly, we want to make an effort to leverage sports to develop youths from disadvantaged backgrounds.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SportSG's philanthropic arm, SportCares, will continue to work with key partners to leverage sport initiatives and programmes to deepen its outreach to vulnerable communities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For instance, Saturday Night Lights (SNL), a flagship SportCares programme since 2013, has served more than 1,000 youths-at-risk or from disadvantaged households.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: These youths develop important life skills such as respect, discipline and resilience through SNL's regular football training and are given a safe and structured space to grow, with coaches acting as their mentors.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will also continue to expand opportunities to students in our schools to access and excel in different sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Today, programmes, such as Strategic Partnership Co-curricular Activities (SP-CCAs) allow students keen to participate in sports not offered as in their schools to do so.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: These include athletics, canoeing, hockey and water polo.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will continue to work with MOE to expand such opportunities for our young.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We are also working to uplift standards so that Singaporeans can take part in sports safely.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For instance, SportSG introduced the National Registry of Exercise Professionals (NREP) in 2023, to build capabilities in the physical fitness sector.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Registered exercise professionals under NREP are certified in areas, such as Standard First Aid and Safe Sport, in addition to their fitness or exercise certifications.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Registered exercise professionals under NREP are also certified in Standard First Aid with Automated External Defibrillator (AED), Safe Sport, Basic Exercise Science or equivalent, so they can better serve Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SportSG is also working with industry partners and Government agencies to establish a Code of Practice for gyms and fitness studios.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This aims to help align best practices in areas, such as equipment and facility management, among other safety considerations for better and more consistent standards across the industry.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I have also set out what we plan to do going ahead.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is to empower SportSG to more effectively administer its role in driving all Singaporeans to live better through sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Hence, we are seeking to make the following amendments in this Bill.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: First, to provide holistic education and career support to our Team Singapore athletes, clause 6(h) of the Bill inserts new section 8(k) and (o).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: These provisions provide an enhanced mandate for SportSG to establish institutions to develop and train national athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This includes overseeing their sporting activities and working with MOE on the Singapore Sports School's (SSP's) academic curricula.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is a key step to implement our plans announced at the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) Committee of Supply (COS) debate in 2025 and will enhance our end-to-end support for our athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We are also laying the groundwork early for the relocation of SSP to Kallang, bringing the school together with sports science facilities, sports medicine centres, national training centres and national sports associations under one roof as the home of a new Team Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: More details on this will be provided at our 2026 COS debate.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Second, to uplift standards of the sports industry, clause 6(h) of the Bill inserts a new section 8(m) and (n) to recognise the leadership role of SportSG in raising the capabilities and safety in the sports sector.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This includes establishing and maintaining quality standards and codes of practice for coaching, equipment, facilities as well as the relevant accreditation systems.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: With the growth in national participation in sports and physical fitness activities, we need to strengthen SportSG's mandate to build capabilities in the sports industry.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Rather than becoming a regulator of the sports industry and taking the approach of regulatory enforcement, SportSG will continue to exercise leadership in the sport sector by encouraging the adoption of industry best practices.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This includes but is not limited to its existing policies and initiatives, such as the Safe Sport Commission, National Registry of Coaches (NROC) and NREP.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Third, to strengthen disability sports and support our effort towards greater inclusivity, clause 6(b) of the Bill seeks to amend section 8(d) of the Act to recognise the Singapore National Paralympic Council (SNPC) as SportSG's key partner, the same way Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC) is recognised today.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is in line with the refreshed DSMP where we have also expanded access and opportunities for persons of all abilities to participate in sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Clause 6(a) of the Bill seeks to amend section 8(a) of the Act to expand the functions of SportSG to expressly include the planning and promotion of physical fitness activities, in addition to sports, for both competitive and recreational purposes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The field of sports science has advanced significantly, and it is now integral to public health initiatives and high-performance sport development both locally and abroad.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Active Health programmes, grounded in sports and exercise science, will also play a larger role in helping our seniors lead longer, stronger and healthier lives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: These amendments signal Singapore's increased commitment to sports science and sports medicine as foundational elements in supporting our nation's next bound in sports and physical fitness activities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Collectively, these moves support Singaporeans' diverse sporting aspirations and is consistent with the wider local and international developments, including at Major Games.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The gameplay and disciplines of mind sports and e-sports will continue to evolve.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Therefore, the updated definition of sports in the Bill takes a balanced and future-ready approach to support newer and more varied forms of sporting participation and sporting excellence by Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SportSG will calibrate its support for these activities and sports based on their specific needs, governance standards and contributions to national sporting objectives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Lastly, the Bill includes and introduces technical amendments to align the Act to the key moves that I have discussed.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It reaffirms that sport is for everyone, regardless of age or ability and our effort for every Singaporean to live better through sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It states, in one voice, our support for Team Singapore athletes and our effort to nurture every athlete to fulfil their fullest sporting potential.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will continue to work closely with partners in the sport ecosystem and industry to ensure smooth implementation of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This Bill touches on a wide and interconnected sporting ecosystem in Singapore and many of my colleagues will be speaking on its various dimensions.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Ms Gho Sze Kee and Ms Valerie Lee will address how we strengthen Team Singapore and disability sport.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Dr Charlene Chen, Mr David Hoe and Ms Elysa Chen will speak on mind sports and e-sports, as well as the importance of governance and accreditation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Ms Poh Li San will speak on the importance of board diversity in our sports associations, while Dr Hamid Razak will address the need for a calibrated and disciplined approach to resource allocation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Lee Hong Chuang will take a broader view across the Bill's themes.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And closing off will be the Deputy Chair of our Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC), Ms Joan Pereira, who will close off the bench's contributions to this debate.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Collectively, these contributions will reflect the breadth of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My remarks today will therefore focus on framing the overall direction of travel, before my colleagues go deeper into the specific policy areas where their suggestions and observations will be made.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: At its very core, this Bill recognises a simple truth, that sport today is not just confine to podiums, pitches or to the playing fields.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is increasingly also about inclusion, health, character, opportunity and lifelong participation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The proposed amendments give SportSG the clarity, mandate and flexibility to meet these realities responsibly.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I will, therefore, focus my remarks on four broad areas: inclusion and disability sport; the broadening of what we recognise as sport; standards and professionalism in our sports ecosystem; and finally, the holistic development of our athletes across sporting and educational pathways.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is alongside the SNOC and the NSAs.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The refreshed DSMP made it clear that inclusion is not an adjunct to our sporting system.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It enables clearer alignment in athlete development, competition pathways and event organisation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It also affirms that disability sport deserves the same strategic attention, resourcing discipline and long-term planning as able-bodied sport.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I would therefore encourage SportSG, as it operationalises this partnership, to continue investing not only in elite pathways, but also in grassroots access.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This includes adaptive facilities, trained coaches and community-level programmes that enable persons with disabilities to engage in sport early and confidently.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Inclusion succeeds not when we create parallel systems, but when our mainstream systems are designed with inclusion in mind from the very beginning.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Bill updates the statutory understanding of what sport is and in doing so, reflects how Singaporeans actually live, train and compete today.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Physical fitness activities are foundational to public health, especially in an ageing society like Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Programmes under ActiveSG, as well as local efforts, such as the North West Healthy Living Festival, recognise that many Singaporeans may not aspire to competitive sport, but still seek structured, social and motivating ways to stay active.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What has also been particularly encouraging is its recent evolution, across all the five Community Development Councils (CDCs).

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: When we invest thoughtfully in simple, inclusive physical activity, we lower the barriers to participation and bring more Singaporeans into physically active lifestyles.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mind sports, such as chess, bridge and e-sports, reflect cognitive skills, discipline and international competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Singapore, as the Minister has described, has hosted various events, such as the World Chess Championships and the Olympic Esports Week as well.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They are globally recognised domains of excellence as well.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: At the same time, I do appreciate the Bill's careful calibration that recognising the sports may not automatically mean equal funding or blanket support.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: SportSG retains the discretion to assess governance standards, athlete pathways and alignment with national objectives.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Public resources must continue to be stewarded carefully and transparently.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I would, however, ask SportSG to continue communicating clearly with the public on how decisions are made, especially when certain popular activities may not receive immediate support, because transparency helps us to build trust, even when not all aspirations can be funded immediately.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Third, Mr Deputy Speaker, on uplifting standards across the sports industry.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Because as participation grows, standards matter more, not less.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Bill provides SportSG with the mandate to establish and maintain quality standards and codes of practice for coaching, equipment, facilities and accreditation systems.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Athletes entrust their bodies and careers to training systems.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Recreational participants as well deserve safe environments and competent instruction.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It allows the sector to mature, to professionalise and to align voluntarily around best practices.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Initiatives, such as the Safe Sport Commission, the NROC and the NREP, have already raised confidence across the ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I would encourage SportSG to continue engaging multiple stakeholders, especially smaller clubs and independent coaches, so that standards uplift rather than exclude.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Over time, Mr Deputy Speaker, as the sector continues to mature, there may be merit in reviewing whether certain baseline protections should become mandatory.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But the present approach, to me, strikes the right balance between leadership and flexibility.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Fourth and lastly, on holistic education and career support for our athletes.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For too long, young athletes have been forced to navigate parallel systems – one focused on sporting excellence; another on academic progression.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Integration therefore allows us to design truly athlete-centric pathways, where education and sports reinforce rather than compete with each other.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The SSP retaining its identity as a school is important.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Education must remain a pillar, not as a concession.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But strengthening its role as the education arm of our high-performance system ensures that sporting ambition does not come at the expense of future options.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It signals a whole-of-ecosystem approach to Team Singapore development, from youth to elite levels.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We will miss the school in the North West district, but we wish it well when it does relocate.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I do look forward to further details at the COS, particularly on how athlete welfare, dual career planning and post-sporting transitions will be strengthened under this consolidated model.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our duty is not just to produce champions but to ensure that those who wear the Singapore crest proudly emerge with dignity, resilience and viable futures beyond sport.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: SportSG's growing role must continue to be exercised with humility, partnership, accountability and transparency.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: The sporting landscape has evolved significantly since the Act was first passed in 1973 and it is only right that our legislative framework reflects modern realities.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: It is a pragmatic step forward to expand the definition of "sport" to include mind sports and e-sports and explicitly incorporate physical fitness activities.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: However, as we expand the remit and powers of the Singapore Sports Council, which is now renamed SportSG, we must ensure that these changes are fiscally sustainable and do not inadvertently stifle the local private sector.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: I have two broad areas of clarification for the Minister: one related to funding dilution and alternative funding streams, and the other to the manufacture of sporting and fitness equipment.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: The expansion of SportSG's functions to include e-sports and mind sports is a significant undertaking.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: These are rapidly growing fields that require specialised infrastructure, coaching and international participation.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: My concern is that if SportSG's budget remains stagnant, we risk diluting the financial support currently available to athletes involved in traditional sports.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: We must ensure that a "win" for e-sports does not come at the cost of a "loss" for other programmes, such as track and field or swimming.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: In light of this, would it be prudent to expand the scope of section 8(d) of the principal Act to explicitly allow SportSG to enter into strategic partnerships with commercial entities and other organisations?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: By leveraging on private sector funding, SportSG can alleviate the burden on the public purse.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: It goes without saying that athlete training is very expensive, as we can see from the experiences of our own Olympic medallists.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: He was supported by a three-year sponsorship agreement with local beverage company, Yeo Hiap Seng, or better known as Yeo's, and the Ng Teng Fong Charitable Foundation, demonstrating how corporate sponsors and external partners can help to chip in to groom more elite athletes for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: I hope that the Ministry and SportSG can develop comprehensive strategies to institutionalise the role of corporate sponsorship in funding athlete training and expand the Sports Excellence Programme (spex) Schemes to support high-performing athletes.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: We need a sustainable model where the state is not the sole benefactor but a facilitator for private sector investment in our sporting talent.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: In addition to the funding perspective, for e-sports specifically, the e-sport ecosystem is unique because the "arenas", namely the games themselves, are intellectual property owned by private publishers.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: To run programmes or tournaments, SportSG will necessitate a different level of commercial engagement than traditional sports.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: How does SportSG intend to navigate these proprietary hurdles?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Traditionally, the Government procures from the private sector to stimulate the economy and benefit from market competition.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: Is there a specific gap in the market that SportSG is trying to fill?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: If SportSG is both the regulator in setting the standards and the supplier in manufacturing the equipment, how do we ensure a level playing field with the private sector?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: How can we avoid a situation where SportSG sets the standards that unfairly disadvantage private competitors?

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: While I support the promotion of physical fitness, I believe the Government should be a catalyst rather than a competitor.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: If SportSG begins manufacturing fitness equipment at scale, it could inadvertently crowd out local retailers and manufacturers who operate on thin margins.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: I hope the Minister can provide assurances that these new powers will be used judiciously and only when the private sector is unable or unwilling to provide the necessary equipment.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: In summary, while I welcome the modernisation of SportSG's remit, we must be wary of over-extension.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: I hope that the Minister can clarify how the Ministry will continue to increase support for our athletes and whether leveraging private sector resources is an active consideration and explain how it intends to use SportSG's powers to regulate and manufacture sports equipment.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The Bill reflects an important recognition that the meaning of sport has evolved in today's society.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Sport is no longer confined to traditional physical competition alone.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: It encompasses physical fitness, high-performance sport, community participation, mind sports and increasingly, e-sports.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: In fact, aside from the Edusave Merit Bursary Award ceremony in my constituency, the other event that attracted so many youths to participate was the e-sports carnival.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: In this respect, the amendments before us are timely and reflect the lived realities of how Singaporeans engage with sports and physical activity.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: This reflects a broader and more inclusive understanding of sport – one that recognises its role not only in elite competition but also in public health, mental well-being and social cohesion.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I have seen first-hand many e-sports groups in my constituency and the role they play, not just in the expanded definition of sports but also in its innate ability to bring people, particularly our youths, together in a productive and positive way to hone and pit their skills against one another, to build communities and deep networks.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: They were, however, usually hampered by a lack of resources and funding, in part because they were measured against the frameworks used for traditional sports.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: This aligns well with our broader efforts to encourage healthier lifestyles and to reduce long-term healthcare costs.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: On that note, this Bill is timely as the aspect of the proposed legislation comes on the back of the recently concluded SEA Games in Thailand where Minister earlier said the Team Singapore did commendably well in several sports, despite some challenges.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: We can see from the public discourse, involving members of the sporting fraternity but engulfing the wider public too, that Singapore expects and desires more for sports.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: We have seen enough in the past decade that our athletes can reach the very top of their fields with the right support, perseverance and opportunities.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: We can certainly do more to support them.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Athletes today face increasingly complex demands – balancing training, education, competition and eventual transition out of sport.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The provision allowing the Council to establish institutions or entities for the development and training of sportspersons, including oversight of their academic progression and curricula with the approval of MOE, also reflects a more integrated and holistic approach to the development of our athletes.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: This should provide flexibility to ensure that the Council has access to a broader range of expertise, including in emerging areas such as e-sports, sports science and physical fitness promotion, while still maintaining sound governance and decision-making processes.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: While I am broadly supportive of the Bill, I would like to raise two points for consideration.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: First, on the inclusion of mind sports and e-sports.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: While their recognition under the Act is appropriate and forward-looking, it will be important to maintain some clarity of purpose and proportionality in how resources, funding and institutional attention are allocated.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Traditional sports, community sports, school sports and disability sports continue to play a critical role in fostering physical health, teamwork, resilience and social integration.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: As new sports such as e-sports grow in prominence, may I seek the assurance of the Minister that the Council will ensure that their development complements rather than crowds out existing sporting pathways, especially those that promote physical activity and broad-based participation.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Clear policy frameworks and differentiated strategies may help ensure that each category of sport is supported in a way that reflects its own distinct objectives and value to society.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: These powers surely can help raise professionalism, safety and quality across the sector.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: However, I would like to caution that their exercise should be calibrated and consultative, particularly where community clubs, volunteers, coaches and small operators are concerned.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: In particular, many in the new sports segments may still be developing and finding their feet and they may lack the track-record, experience, capabilities and resources at the same levels of more established sports organisations.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Sport is most effective when it is embedded within communities and when national strategy is complemented by local ownership and ground-up energy.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Sports in Singapore should always be accessible to all and not just the mandate of the elite professionals.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: (In Tamil):  Hon Deputy Speaker, when the great poet Mahakavi Bharathiyar sang "Run and play, child" he celebrated the joy and freedom of sports.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Starting with childhood and throughout life, sports strengthen us physically and mentally.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: This Bill fortifies the belief that sports should be attainable by all despite age, skill or whatever one's background may be.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I wholeheartedly welcome this effort that brings communities together towards a common ground that fosters sports.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: They competed with heart, dedication and unwavering commitment to excellence.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Every athlete who wore our national colours deserves our recognition and gratitude.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: They trained countless hours, made personal sacrifices and gave their absolute best for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Yet, Mr Deputy Speaker, pride in our athletes' efforts must be accompanied by honest reflection on our sporting ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Singapore's medal tally and rankings demonstrate that despite investments over the years, we continued to face challenges in developing consistent sporting excellence across disciplines.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: When we compare our performance to regional neighbours, some with fewer resources but more strategic focus, it becomes clear that our current model requires serious examination.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: This is the context in which we consider the Singapore Sports Council (Amendment) Bill 2025.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: This Bill represents a significant evolution in how Singapore approaches sport, competition and athlete development.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: While I support the overall direction and intent of these reforms, I believe we must scrutinise the details carefully to ensure that good intentions translate into effective governance and tangible outcomes for our sporting community, outcomes that our athletes deserve.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: The Bill defines Mind Sports as a competitive game based on intellectual skill rather than physical skill such as chess or bridge.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: For too long, we have conflated sport with purely physical activity.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Yet, the chess player who trains for hours daily, analysing positions and studying strategy, demonstrates the same dedication, discipline and competitive spirit as any athlete.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: The bridge player who competes at international level exhibits mental stamina and strategic thinking that will challenge any sports person.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: By bringing Mind Sports explicitly under SportSG mandate, we create formal pathways for these athletes – access to coaching standards and the possibility of structured support.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: The expansion by 10 additional members suggests the Government recognises the wider variety of sports and activities now falling under SportSG's purview.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: This is logical given we are adding mind sports and e-sports to the mix.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: But I must ask what is the strategic purpose of such a large Council?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: From a governance perspective, larger councils are typically less effective, not more.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Decision-making becomes slower, coordination more complex and accountability more diffuse.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: There is nothing preventing SportSG from establishing sub-councils or sport-specific working groups with external experts co-opted on an ad hoc basis.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: A lean engaged Council of 15 will serve Singapore's sporting community far better than the sprawling body of 25 where attendance is optional.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Our SEA Games performance demonstrates that we need decisive focused leadership, not a committee too large to be effective.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Our athletes deserve better governance, not bigger committee.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: This appears to pave the way for significant institutional restructuring.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Are there other sport excellence schools planned in the pipeline that would similarly fall under SportSG's management?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: If so, what is being done to beef up the capabilities of the SportSG to take on these substantial new responsibilities?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Managing educational institutions requires expertise in pedagogy, student welfare and academic administration, not just sports development.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Our performance at the 2025 Games provides a real-world benchmark.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Despite years of investment and institutional development, what tangible improvements have we seen?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Where are the success stories that justify continued investment in the current model?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: And where are the failures that demand course correction.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Without this accountability for past spending, how can we have confidence in the expanded mandate proposed under this Bill?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: And without understanding what worked and what did not, how can we allocate future resources wisely?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Our athletes who completed at SEA Games 2025 worked with the system we gave them.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: If that system underperformed, the responsibility lies not with them, but with us, with the structures, funding and strategic direction we provided.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: We owe them answers before we ask them to trust a new expanded system.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: This is genuinely welcome and represents a more holistic approach to athlete welfare.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: For too long, talented young Singaporeans have hesitated to pursue sporting excellence because they feared an uncertain future after retirement.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: By providing structured educational pathways and career transition support, we make sports a viable life choice, not a risky gamble.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: This will unlock talent that currently goes untapped.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Perhaps, if we have implemented such support earlier, we might have retained more athletes who could have contributed to stronger SEA Games' performances.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: How many potential medalists chose safer career paths because the sporting pathway seems too precarious?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: However, I must ask, what about our past athletes?

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Many former national athletes, including those who represented us at previous SEA Games, struggle after retirement.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Having sacrificed their peak earning years and educational opportunities for Singapore's sporting glory, some face financial difficulties, struggle to enter the workforce or lack credentials for career advancement.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: They deserve consideration, not just those who benefit from future systems.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: These are athletes who paved the way, who competed when support was even more limited than it is today.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: These are athletes who have represented Singapore with pride, who have stood on podiums wearing our flag.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Our 2025 SEA Games athletes and those who came before them surely deserve more that career counselling.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: We can provide concrete financial instruments that secure their futures.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: But progress requires not just good intentions but sound governance and demonstrated accountability.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: A Council of 25 is a recipe for inefficiency.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Expanded institutional responsibilities without demonstrated capability and accountability for past spending is putting the cart before the horse.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Our performance at the 2025 SEA Games should serve as a wake-up call.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: We cannot continue expanding mandates without first addressing the fundamental issues that have limited our sporting success.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Now we must ensure that our institutions match their commitment with excellence of our own.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: I urge the Minister to address these concerns directly.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Show us the performance analysis from SEA Games: explain what went wrong and what will change.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: We continue to believe that those who have already given their best years to Singapore's sporting glory deserve the same consideration in our promise to future athletes.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Let us pass a Bill that is not just forward looking but also well-governed, adequately resourced, accountable and fair to all who have contributed to Singapore's sporting legacy.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Let us ensure that when we host or compete in future regional Games, we can point to this legislation as a turning point that led to sustained sporting excellence.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Now it is time for us to do ours.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Yes, Mr Deputy Speaker, just two clarifications for the hon Member.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I note in his speech that he used the words that he proposes amendment, in terms of the size of the Council.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: That is way more than what we had in 2023.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: So, I am not sure how he came to the conclusion that we did not perform better in 2025.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik, would you like to respond to the hon Member Mr Yam?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Do you have clarifications arising out of what the Member said?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: With regard to his clarification on the performance, I would like to clarify with him if it is accurate to say that he is referring to specific performances of specific sports during the SEA Games, rather than the overall performance which was markedly better in 2025 than in previous SEA Games.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: They have flown our flag high and done our country proud.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Their performance is a fitting backdrop for the passage of this particular Bill in the House and at this juncture I would also extend my best wishes to Team Singapore at the ASEAN Para Games next week.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Mountbatten is where many of our national sportsmen and sportswomen train, the home base of many NSAs and the Singapore National Olympic Council, the Singapore Disability Sports Council and SportSG itself.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: I especially look forward to the realisation of the Kallang Alive Master Plan when the Singapore Sports School will also find a new home in Mountbatten.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: We should acknowledge that the Government has done a great deal for sports in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: One only needs to take a walk around the Kallang precinct to see the physical embodiment of the Government's support and commitment.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: And it is not just the physical facilities and hardware.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: We have also built a very comprehensive support system for our high performance athletes, one which supports them from the start of their sporting career journey through their transition into a second career.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Today, the various spex schemes support our athletes.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Emerging athletes can receive a smaller amount through spexPotential.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Non-full-time athletes can receive spexTraining Assistance Grants and tap into spexGLOW, which provides monetary offsets for loss of income for athletes taking time off in the run up to Major Games.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: There is also spexEducation for athletes to pursue tertiary studies during or after their sports career and spexCareer to help athletes transition into new careers after sports.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: This underscores the Government's commitment and resolve to support our sports ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: And yet, there have been many calls for the Government to do more, more and yet more for sports in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: To show more commitment, to provide further support to sports and our athletes.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Much has been said about how Singapore can win more medals.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: There are a few thoughts that I must share.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But then so too would $1 billion, $2 billion, or $4 billion be not enough.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: We must always keep in mind the big picture.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Our national resources are finite and there are many competing priorities of Government that are essential to our nation: defence, education, healthcare, transport, homeland security, national infrastructure, housing, the environment and so on.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Indeed, even for MCCY itself, sports is just one aspect of their broader remit that also includes our arts scene, community and youths.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: While support for sports is important, it must be balanced against the broader national responsibilities and prudent allocation of resources.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Next, we must also keep in mind that SportSG's mandate is not just limited to high performance sports and medal tallies alone.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: SportSG also has the larger social and community mission of fostering inclusion, cohesion and bonding through sports, as well as encouraging personal character building and fostering an active, healthy lifestyle in the larger community.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: The payout to our society from this mission is just as meaningful and important to our society as nurturing medal winning athletes, if not more so.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Intra community sporting events such as the Pesta Sukan and the Singapore Urban Sports and Fitness Festival, our ActiveSG framework, public sports facilities like our neighbourhood swimming pools and stadiums are all part of this mission.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: The other point is the cold hard reality of elite competitive sports.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: For every podium finisher and every gold medal, many more would have fallen short by the wayside.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: This is something that we must confront honestly.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Physical ageing is a reality for every one of us, athletes included.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: This is the reality many of our athletes face.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Yet many postpone, disrupt or forgo education and career development during their peak years in order to pursue excellence in sports.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: It is an enormous personal sacrifice and takes grit and courage.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Our focus therefore cannot be limited to how athletes perform during their competitive years alone but also must extend to how they emerge after them.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: To me, the benchmark of our support of our athletes should never be the number of medals they have won.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: I note that SportSG has already does this.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Its support ecosystem that provides holistic education and career transition assistance to athletes is especially commendable.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: To me, the most important sub programmes within the spex framework are spexEducation and spexCareer because these programmes are designed to equip our athletes with the qualifications, skills and pathways to successfully transition into post sports life.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: I look forward to further announcements on such holistic support for our athletes that will be forthcoming in the Committee of Supply debates.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: A common theme that often arises in this House when we discuss support for sports and athletes is that it takes a village.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: When it comes to funding and resources, that village naturally includes the corporate world.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Another invariable point is the disparity in medal prize money awarded for the Olympics and the Paralympics.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Our corporate world can and should do much more.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: But since we have been on hard truths and harsh realities, I would like to offer up more of them.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: The hard truth is that we are a tiny country.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Our size translates to a small commercial audience and domestic market.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: That makes the commercialisation of professional sports and athletes difficult.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: The struggles of the S League demonstrate this.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Our corporate world, too, despite our outsized economy, is quite small, with a correspondingly small sponsorship pie.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Too many others have already done so but allow me to float an idea.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: A merger between them will be the natural next step.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: There are many advantages to such a merger.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: At a minimum, it would reduce duplication of effort and allow the sharing of common resources, saving costs.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: More importantly, a merged body will make corporate funding easier and strategic by presenting a large and unified front to sponsors.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Within this unified entity, we shall no longer see two separate and different sized and medal sized pools.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Furthermore, such a merger already has a public face.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: There already exists a unified corporate identity in Team Singapore, which brings Olympics and Paralympics athletes together under one marketing banner.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: I hope MCCY, SportSG and the respective councils can give this idea some serious consideration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I do want to also congratulate our Team Singapore athletes at the recent SEA Games.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I spent 10 days with them and cheering them on.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: So, I do apologise as my voice is still recovering from those 10 days of cheering.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I do want to also declare my interest as the President of Singapore Aquatics, an NSA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: In supporting this Bill, I will focus on three areas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: First, how we expand participation and inclusion in ways that strengthen our sporting base; second, why uplifting standards and professionalising coaching are essential as participation grows; and third, why high-performance sport remains vital, not just for medals, but for the values it inculcates in society and the sense of who we are as a nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: This recognises that structured competitive activities can take different forms and allows more Singaporeans, across different interests, abilities and life circumstances to participate meaningfully in sport, whether recreationally or at higher levels.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: The Singapore Chess Federation, for example, runs regular programmes in prisons and in rehabilitation settings, showing how mind sports, like chess, can provide structure, discipline and engagement even in higher constrained environments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: In the same spirit of inclusivity, I also strongly support the continued emphasis on disability sports through the recognition of the SNPC as a key partner.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: This amendment, together with the refreshed DSMP signals a sustained commitment to ensuring that sport remains accessible and meaningful for Singaporeans of all abilities and affirms inclusion as a core principle of our sporting ecosystem.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: For Singaporeans who may not be drawn to organised sport, but simply want to stay active, bringing the promotion of physical fitness squarely within SportSG's functions is critical.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: It allows SportSG to lead in creating accessible everyday opportunities for Singaporeans to keep active from neighbourhood ActiveSG programmes to platforms, like the Singapore Urban Sports and Fitness Festival.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: So, taken together, these developments help Singaporeans stay active.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: They help them bond and it helps us strengthen our resilience in the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: But as participation grows, ensuring sport is safe and well conducted becomes even more important.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Coaching quality, facility standards and codes of conduct matter even more, not just for performance, but for safety and longer-term participation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: In particular, professionalising coaching at the developmental level is critical, as research shows that early experiences strongly influence whether young people remain engaged in sport.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: And so, this is why initiatives, like the NROC, matter.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: The certification is meant to signal professional standards and support better remuneration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: But its impact is limited when certification is not consistently required across all instances where sports coaching is practised.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, a coach whose NROC registration is suspended may be restricted from coaching at ActiveSG facilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: But they can still coach in a privately-owned non-ActiveSG facility.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Without the stronger reach to uphold standards, the professionalisation of sports coaching is weakened and, more crucially, it also puts our young athletes at risk.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: This is important in context involving youth instruction where safety and proper conduct are paramount.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: In the meantime, uplifting standards must remain a shared responsibility.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Our NSAs already work with SportSG to require NROC certification for official roles in NSA-sanction activities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I know in schools as well, many schools require coaches with NROC certification.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: But the clubs, sporting organisations, they can also make recognised certification a requirement when engaging coaches.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: They can ask about certification, encourage coaches to attend professional development courses organised by SportSG or CoachSG, and support remuneration that reflects a coach's training and qualifications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: This brings me to a related point about how athlete development is organised under this Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: I support the intent behind clause 6(k) which empowers SportSG to develop and train sports persons, particularly at the national and elite levels where a more centralised approach can strengthen high performance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: But at the same time, I seek assurance and clarification on how this role will be exercised alongside existing developmental pathways.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: In several sports, early-stage development is already being carried out by private clubs and private organisations working closely with the NSAs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: They play an important role in building the pipeline.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: In particular, I would appreciate clarification on how SportSG intends to work with NSAs to identify and support credible development partners that are aligned with national objectives, meet governance and safeguarding standards and contribute meaningfully to athlete development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: We must, therefore, continue to remain attentive to how we support those who represent the nation at the highest levels.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Excellence and Major Games, such as the Olympics, play a unique role in our national consciousness.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: It builds pride and creates moments of collective unity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Many of us will remember Joseph Schooling's gold medal at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: It was not just that he won, but how he won, defeating the legendary Michael Phelps in a race that ended in a rare three-way tie for silver.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: That race reminded Singaporeans that, on the biggest stage, against the greatest in the world, we can still make our mark.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: More recently and closer to home, at the SEA Games, we witnessed that same inspiration expressed in different ways.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: We saw history made as hurdler Calvin Quek and diver Avvir Tham, each ended longstanding gold medal droughts for Singapore in their respective events, achievements not seen since our Independence in 1965.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: But high performance sport is not only about individual triumphs or podium finishes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: It is also about how athletes respond when their team needs them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: In men's table tennis, Josh Chua was stretched off after twisting his left ankle.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, he chose to return to the court and played on, determined to contribute whatever he could for the team.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: While he might have lost his game, that decision to carry on despite being injured, had a galvanising impact which lifted his teammates Koen Pang and Izaac Quek, who themselves were battling illness and injury and helping Team Singapore retain the gold in the men's team event.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Team work is about putting the team above itself, even in sports, like swimming, that are often seen as individual.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: We are familiar with the women's four by 100-metre medley relay at the SEA Games which illustrates this powerfully where we saw our senior swimmers Letitia Sim, Quah Ting Wen and Quah Jing Wen supporting 14-year-old debutant Julia Yeo, who was notified at the last minute to swim in place of an injured teammate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: But what was less known was that at the same time that Julia was called, another reserve for the relay, 15-year-old Victoria Lim, also a SEA Games debutant, was also asked to stand by to compete in what would have been the biggest race of her career.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Ultimately, the decision was made to go with Julia.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: We know the team won and so she lost out on having that chance for the gold medal as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, Victoria accepted the decision with quiet stoicism.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: She put the team ahead of her own disappointments and stood firmly behind her teammates without hesitation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: After a short vacation, she was back in the pool, more determined than ever to represent Team Singapore at Major Games and to make the nation proud.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: But that moment, for me, it captures what a "we first" Singapore looks like.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: Putting the Team first sometimes means being prepared to step aside, even at personal loss, so that the Team can succeed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: And it is precisely because high-performance sport carries this national meaning and because it is inherently resource-intensive, we must approach it with focus and intent.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: And so, even as we expand opportunities for participation and inclusion, we must be careful not to spread ourselves too thin.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: This calls for a pragmatic strategic approach, guided by a long-term view of elite sport development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: So, if in the spirit of inclusion, we want to support a wider range of emerging sports, and if, in the spirit of excellence, we also want to sustain high performance competitive sport, then we must expand the pool of funding available to the sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: This is a significant and forward looking move.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: While education and high performance sport require different professional expertise, for athletes, many of whom are still in school, these domains are deeply entangled.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: As a former national athlete myself, I can attest that these were challenges that I faced awhile back when I was still an athlete and it is an issue that our athletes still face today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: And so, it is commendable that SportSG is actively addressing this issue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: It broadens participation and inclusion, uplift standards and professionalism and sustains high performance sports, so that it inspires us as one united people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
text: For these reasons, I support the Singapore Sports Council (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: From one national athlete to a competitive bowler.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
