text: Mind sports foster social connection, reduce isolation and provide structured competitive outlets that build community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could the Ministry consider making it a goal to tap on mind sports to support active ageing objectives, by providing more avenues and opportunities for our seniors to remain mentally active as well?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How will SportSG leverage mind sports to engage seniors and foster inter-generational bonding?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   For seniors, the benefits of mind sports extend beyond recreation.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Research shows that cognitively engaging activities like chess reduce the risk of cognitive decline.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mind sports foster social connection, reduce isolation, and provide competitive outlets that build community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could the Ministry consider making it a goal to tap on mind sports to support active ageing objectives, by providing more opportunities for our seniors to remain mentally active as well?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How will SportSG leverage mind sports to engage seniors and foster inter-generational bonding?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): Second, engaging our youths through an evolving sports scene.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our youths are active in an ever-evolving sports scene.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is a growing sector that commands massive audiences.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The much-needed formal acknowledgment will pave the way for funding their training and participation at regional and international competitions, enabling them to hone their skills.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The attractive prize rewards will make their pursuits a viable sporting career, like other more traditional sports.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Third, uplifting professionalism by making sport a viable career.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One of the most important component of this Bill is to uplift the professionalism of sport and make it a viable, long-term career option for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Official recognition provides athletes with support and development pathways.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For Singapore to build a vibrant sports ecosystem, we must signal clearly that sports, in all its forms, can be a credible, sustainable career.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our talented athletes need more financial and institutional support to attain excellence in order to pursue sports professionally.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am heartened that this Bill aims to addresses that gap through three key mechanisms.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The new model signals holistic support through education, career transitions and life after sport.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Minister share in greater detail the measures to support athletes in their lives after their sports career end?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Third, recognition of e-sports and mind sports creates entirely new career paths.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Government be able to consider introducing training schemes to develop talents in this sector?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Fourth, expanding flexible sports facilities while managing disamenities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is not merely about convenience, it is about removing barriers to participation and embedding sports into the daily community life.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, expanding access must be balanced with residents' quality of life.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, the rise of pickleball illustrates the tension vividly.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There were many complaints about pickleball noise in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents, especially night shift workers, have reported being disturbed by the distinctive sound of pickleball.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There have also been complaints by residents living in the proximity of other sports facilities, such as basketball courts.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Besides closing the courts and switching lights off earlier, signs remind players to be considerate and keep noise down, and town councils encourage the use of quieter sports equipment.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While these ground-up responses are commendable, as we expand facilities under the Sports Facilities Master Plan, we must proactively design for noise mitigation and considerate use.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This means incorporating acoustic buffers and scheduling guidelines into design and fostering a culture of mutual respect between players and residents.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Not only that, such a facility will encourage more young people to explore their talents in ice sports and provide a fun place for families to enjoy and stay active.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It recognises that sport serves multiple purposes: first, keeping seniors cognitively engaged; second, connecting with youth through formats they find meaningful; third, creating viable career pathways for athletes and coaches; and fourth, providing accessible, flexible facilities in every neighbourhood.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will encourage all residents, young and old, to participate meaningfully in our sporting culture.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Several Members in the House spoke about how we can support our athletes better, during and after their careers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Alex Yam, Ms Gho Sze Kee, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Ms Joan Pereira spoke about support for athletes' transition to life after sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our athletes have similar aspirations to many Singaporeans – they want to pursue higher educational qualifications, start and grow their careers and work towards financial stability.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Ms Valerie Lee asked about the selection criteria.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We focus our resources on supporting our full-time spexScholars who are best able to benefit from this scholarship, including the daily training environment that their Institute of Higher Learning provides if they are studying and competing at the same time.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Or if they intend to study only after they retire from competitive sports, then we consider the course that they are pursuing and the potential future contributions to the sports sector.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: One such example is Jessica Tan, our mixed doubles badminton Olympian and 2022 Commonwealth champion.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: After a very successful career, Jessica retired last year and she is now pursuing a degree in sport management and coaching.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: After her graduation, she will return back to contribute to our sports sector.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: On top of that, they now receive Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-ups, bolstering their finances to better meet their housing, medical and retirement needs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked about support for former national athletes, including healthcare.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We support our athletes' transition into retirement from their competitive sporting careers by helping them find good employment.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Active and retired athletes can also tap on various programmes, including spexBusiness and spexEducation, which I mentioned, and we have recently enhanced.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In addition, there are national schemes to support healthcare and other needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For example, our public healthcare financing system, the S+3Ms – namely subsidies, MediShield Life, MediSave and MediFund – help keeps healthcare affordable for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Dr Charlene Chen spoke about supporting our athletes' mental well-being.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The High Performance Sport Institute proactively monitors our athletes' mental health and provides them with support throughout their sporting career.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: With a dedicated Athlete Life Management team, the High Performance Sport Institute equips our athletes for life, helping them develop the skills and mental resilience needed to deal with life's challenges, including after retirement from sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Through this entity, we will strengthen our partnerships with key stakeholders in the High Performance Sport ecosystem, bringing together different specialists in their fields, for example, coaches, psychologists, athlete-life managers and sport administrators, in a clear, comprehensive way to provide wrap-around support for our athletes, helping them stay in competitive sports for as long as they can.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I agree with Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh and Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim on the benefits of integration, and their support for us to bring the Singapore Sports School to Kallang and integrate all elements of the High Performance Sport ecosystem under one roof in the new home of Team Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: To Ms Elysa Chan's question on accountability, I would like to assure the Member that the entity will still be funded by the Government and be accountable to the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and Parliament.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: With the consolidation, the Singapore Sports School remains a specialised independent school and will continue receiving support from both MOE and MCCY.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The Singapore Sports School will continue to provide education to national and aspiring athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Besides serving the academic needs of student-athletes, the Singapore Sports School will expand its role to provide career guidance support to other national athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The excellent track record of our Team Singapore athletes gives us confidence that our sporting ecosystem is developing in the right direction.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Shuttler and Singapore Sports School alumnus, Loh Kean Yew, became Singapore's first-ever badminton world champion at the 2021 BWF World Championships.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our most decorated Paralympian, Yip Pin Xiu, is a seven-time Paralympic gold medallist and eight-time World Champion, with two world records to her name.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our kite foiling sensation, Max Maeder, is a double world champion, and won Bronze at his Olympic debut in Paris 2024.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: His other accolades include winning Gold thrice at the Trofeo Princesa Sofia Regatta, two Golds and a Silver at the Formula Kite World Championships, and an Asian Games Gold at Hangzhou 2022.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Amanda Yap become Singapore's first-ever gymnast to reach a World Championships Final and placed sixth at the 2025 Artistic Gymnastics World Championship.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In bowling, Singapore Sports School alumni, Darren Ong, made history as the first male Singaporean bowler to claim the Men's Singles title at the 2023 IBF World Championships since 2006.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And at the same championships, sisters Cherie and Daphne Tan shared a special moment, winning the women's doubles gold medal.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In silat, we have Sheik Farhan Sheik Alau'ddin, our five-time world champion who secured multiple world titles at events, such as the World Pencak Silat Championships.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In wushu, Singapore Sports School student-athlete Zeanne Law was crowned World Champion twice in Women's Taijiquan in 2023 and 2024.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And at the 2023 World Wushu Championships, Singapore Sports School alumnus Jowen Lim won his first world championship title in "gunshu".

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I cite all these achievements because I do not want us to be mistaken that we think the system is working well just because we had a record medal haul in the SEA Games.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The system is working well because our athletes have done us proud at all the different world level competitions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We all have a part to play in growing sports excellence in Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As a small nation with a small talent base, we are competing with nations who are multiple times larger than us, and with budgets that are significant and increasing.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our approach has always been one to partner with all stakeholders and complement each other's strengths, as Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh pointed out, so that we can maximise our investments.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The amendment to section 8(d) of the Act reflects this, where we are shifting from consultation to working in partnership with stakeholders to bring about better outcomes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The National Sport Associations (NSAs) play an important role in promoting and uplifting their respective sports, and many NSAs have done good work with their grassroots and through their developmental programmes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Coaches play a pivotal role in shaping both athletic performance and the broader sporting environment.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Ms Joan Pereira made several sound suggestions on recruiting and developing coaches.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: MCCY and SportSG continually review our coach education and development programmes under CoachSG, with a view to building a deep and sustainable pipeline of coaching talents to support our athletes to achieve our High Performance Sport ambition, as well as to provide clear development and progression pathways, from grassroots to high performance coaches for elite athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is in line with our tiered coaching pathways as guided by a competency framework.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Various Members also spoke about the importance of having good access to sports facilities and the challenges that some residents face in booking public courts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Today, through the Sport Facilities Master Plan, Singaporeans can access public sports facilities near to where they live.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We provide a mix of larger sport centres in towns and smaller facilities in our neighbourhoods for easy access, particularly for seniors and young families.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Given the scarcity of land in Singapore, we have been innovative by activating underutilised spaces.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Rooftops of multi storey carparks are also being repurposed as recreational spaces, such as the upcoming facility in Dover Crescent.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will also continue to explore and partner others to open up more spaces for play and tapping on existing collaborations, like the Dual-Use Scheme with schools.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I agree with Ms Valerie Lee that our sports facilities should serve the needs of a broad range of entities, in addition to our national sports associations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: So, for example, our ActiveSG facilities and facilities at The Kallang are used by community sports groups, grassroots organisations, schools and corporates to host events and activities, such as the National School Games, Sport Days, community carnivals, festivals, sports competitions and charity events, like Football with a Heart.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Yip Hon Weng suggested having a code of practice for sports facilities in HDB estates.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Well, our approach is not to be overly prescriptive and allow flexibility to accommodate residents' preferences, given that each precinct in Singapore is a little bit different.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: At the same time, SportSG will work with all the relevant stakeholders, including the NSAs and, where possible, consider other solutions in terms of facility design or choice of equipment.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will work within our land constraints and we will continue to find innovative ways of providing public access to a diverse mix of sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked whether there will be a new ice rink.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SportSG and other agencies have been working closely with the ice sport NSAs on this matter.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In the same spirit, we will continue to partner with respective NSAs to support our athletes' short- and long-term training needs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I am glad to hear Members’ support for recognising a more diverse group of sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Recognition can help them increase membership, develop talent and secure funding or sponsorship.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Some of these newer sports will also catalyse the supporting industries.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For example, in the area of e-sports, create more demand for software developers and graphic designers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Instead, our focus is on supporting the diverse interests of Singaporeans, so that we can promote and develop sports in Singapore and as Ms Poh Li San said – to uplift and bond our nation through sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We welcome suggestions to make this clearer to interested stakeholders and will continue to engage the sector closely.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And to Mr David Hoe, I have to say that for something to be considered a mind sport, it needs to be affiliated to an NSA, who is in turn affiliated to an International Federation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: So, I do not think Toto will make the list anytime soon.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I would also like to assure Mr Fadli Fawzi that SportSG will continue to work with commercial entities to support a more vibrant and diverse sporting ecosystem.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The recognition of more sports also offers an opportunity to engage various segments of population in different ways as Ms Joan Pereira has pointed out.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Seniors can be engaged through mind sports to keep them mentally and socially active, which will complement today’s physical activity programmes offered by Government agencies and community partners.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Indeed, as Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr David Hoe pointed out too, there is also an opportunity to engage youths through e-sports, given its popularity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I agree with Dr Charlene Chen, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr David Hoe that we should do so while addressing all the possible risks, such as potential issues with regard to gaming addiction.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will work with industry and community partners such as the Singapore Cybersports and Online Gaming Association and the Singapore Esports Association, as well as Government agencies like MOE and MOH to do so.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I agree with Ms Valerie Lee, Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim, Mr David Hoe and Dr Hamid Razak that the development of new sports, including e-sports should complement rather than crowd out existing sporting pathways, especially those that promote physical activity and broad-based participation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As Dr Charlene Chen pointed out, one such pathway is the Direct School Admission (DSA).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: MOE schools have the autonomy to offer programmes that suit their students' needs and interests.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: MOE prioritises physical sports in the National School Games as movement and regular physical activity are fundamental to students' holistic development and health.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For other types of sports, there are competition platforms organised by various organisations for students to represent their schools.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Members including Mr Alex Yam, Mr Lee Hong Chuang, Dr Kenneth Goh, Mr David Hoe, Ms Elysa Chan also talked about our funding principles.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Broadly, we calibrate the amount of support for sports based on their specific needs, governance standards and contribution to our national sporting objectives, which includes the ability of the sport and its competition to inspire the Singapore spirit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We regularly review our support for sports and will continue to engage with the NSAs and other partners, like Singapore National Olympic Council and Singapore National Paralympic Council, so that we can collectively move in the same direction to uplift Singapore sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Lee Hong Chuang, Mr Fadli Fawzi asked how we would ensure fiscal sustainability.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And we will make sport more accessible and inclusive for everyone.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: That is why we refreshed the Disability Sports Master Plan (DSMP) in 2024 to raise sport participation for persons with disabilities, focusing on three key strategic themes: First, to increase accessibility to disability sports programmes and activities; second, to enhance awareness of disability sports and inclusive sports activities, and; third, fulfil aspirations of persons with disabilities who desire and have the potential to do sports at the high performance level.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will work closely with various partners like schools, sports associations and community partners to implement the various strategic moves as laid out in the DSMP.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Ms Gho Sze Kee suggested the merging of the Singapore National Olympic Council and the Singapore National Paralympic Council.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Both councils are independent and have their respective missions of developing and promoting the Olympic and Paralympic movements respectively, and amongst others, preparing our athletes for major games.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I am sure they will take to heart the suggestion.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: There will be benefits with the current arrangement and there will be other possible benefits with a merger.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And it comes down to which structure will allow them to meet their mandate and mission better and which structure serves Singapore and Team Singapore better.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Both councils have done great work in uplifting sports and athletes in their sectors and MCCY and SportSG will continue working closely with them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I would also like to thank Ms Poh Li San, Dr Hamid Razak and Dr Charlene Chen for their suggestions on ensuring a wider representation of professionals or experts in sports education, disability sports, sports psychology, sports tourism, community sports and senior sports on the Board of SportSG.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is in line with our plans to diversify SportSG Board’s expertise to enable it to lead the sport sector well.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The maximum of 25 members on the Board of SportSG provides us the scope to bring on board more diverse expertise and perspectives, and is in line with the size of other Statutory Boards.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is a maximum number, it is not a target, and we will continue to ensure that the Board runs effectively and efficiently.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It is imperative that we work together to keep our seniors active and healthy through sports and physical fitness activities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Members Mr Alex Yam, Dr Charlene Chen and Mr David Hoe as well as Ms Joan Pereira have raised this.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: One key initiative is the Frailty Prevention Programme (FPP) that we have been progressively introducing to our Active Ageing Centres (AACs).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: There are two key components to the FPP.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: First, the Combat Age-Related Loss of Muscle programme (CALM), which is an eight-week programme targeted at seniors to help them understand muscle health through assessment, guided strength training, and health coaching.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: After going through CALM, almost all seniors reported an improvement in at least one of five measurements, with at least 85% of them improving in at least three of these measurements.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will continue to run more runs of CALM and consider expanding them to the Residents Network as well should there be interest.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Second, introducing adaptive sports to seniors in AACs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Some Members also asked about helping children and youth from disadvantaged backgrounds access sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Sport can provide a safe and structured environment for them to build confidence, resilience and stronger connection to friends and society.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SportSG provides a SportCares Bursary for children and youths from low-income families to participate in ActiveSG Academies and Clubs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will continue to work closely with stakeholders and community partners to identify suitable children and youths for our initiatives and ensure that more can benefit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SportSG will also continue to design and administer grants and programmes that can benefit different segments of the population, to strengthen our ecosystem or increase access to sport.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This has played a vital role in supporting smaller organisations like Amplify, enabling them to create meaningful change in the lives of vulnerable communities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Through their functional fitness program, Amplify empowers youth at risk, seniors, and persons with disabilities by promoting holistic wellness and fostering a sense of community.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Beneficiaries develop physical strength, resilience, and leadership skills, while gaining valuable industry knowledge for future employment opportunities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We are also working to ensure that our people engage in physical fitness activities safely.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I am encouraged by the Members’ support towards SportSG’s calibrated approach.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As Mr Alex Yam, Dr Hamid Razak, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Lee Hong Chuang and Dr Charlene Chen pointed out, over-regulation would deter smaller players or grassroots groups.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our current focus is to ensure baseline standards and eventually uplift the sector.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: These are not intended to be onerous but are simple and essential requirements for a more developed industry for Singaporeans’ benefit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will continue to review our approach and engage the sector.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked about a potential conflict of interest SportSG’s expanded function to manufacture and supply sport and physical equipment, as well as to set standards for such equipment in clause 6(m) and 6(l) of the Bill.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: To clarify, SportSG typically does not manufacture sports or physical fitness equipment for sale.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Items provided are usually meant to provide a service to Singaporeans, such as gym towels or water-bottles for children.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: SportSG also periodically provides sport-related items such as sport-resistance bands or TeamSG premiums, as part of its role to promote an active lifestyle or to strengthen public support for Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Ms Elysa Chen asked about the accountability of standards set and approvals given.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The criteria for being registered on the National Registry of Coaches and National Registry of Exercise Professionals and the names of coaches and exercise professionals is listed on the respective registries and publicly available.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The requirements for accreditation are also objective, such as first aid certification.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We are on the right track to scale the next bound of sports in Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Second, we are transforming our “software” to support our youth and senior athletes holistically with deeper investments in sports science and sports medicine and stronger partnerships with our NSAs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Third, we have set out a masterplan and we are running programmes and initiatives to be more inclusive through sport by empowering persons with disabilities, outreaching to vulnerable youths and supporting students of all abilities to provide good access sports in schools and to nurture a love for sport from young.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Last but not least, we are setting standards to ensure our people engage in physical activities safely, so that Singaporeans can lead active and healthy lifestyles.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: At this juncture, I also want to thank Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Lee Hong Chuang, Ms Poh Li San and Dr Kenneth Goh for reminding us that sport at any level is not just about winning and doing well.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It is also about inculcating values, building character and giving ourselves a sense of who we are as a nation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It is about how we respond when our team needs us.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Dr Kenneth Goh gave us the examples of Josh Chua, Koen Pang, Izaac Quek and Victoria Lim putting team before self and nation before self.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And there were many more examples that we witnessed at the many sporting events, in our schools and communities as well.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It is about how we respond in defeat.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: While we had a record medal haul at the SEA Games, we had our share of disappointments as well.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our netball team, who are Asian youth champions, suffered an agonising three-point loss in the finals.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: There will be good days and there will be bad days.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: What matters is we always come back, stronger.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: That is how our support for our athletes should be.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We support them when they are doing well and we support them even more if they are not doing well.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: That is how sport bonds and uplifts us as a nation – not because we win all the time, but because we know how difficult it is to win and we always come back, stronger.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: From providing more support for our athletes beyond sports, participating actively in our lineup of programmes, stepping forward to contribute to a vibrant and inclusive sporting ecosystem, there is a role for everyone.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: There is much to look forward to for Singapore's sports.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will continue to work closely with all stakeholders to implement this Bill effectively and ensure that our national sport ecosystem remains inclusive, dynamic and future-ready.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Looks like it is a very comprehensive round-up.
